summary: No blocking issues were confirmed in the inspected workspace. The round-4 sidebar/list UX is implemented, core round-3 behavior still holds, automated checks pass, and the only remaining gap I saw is the still-unrun real-browser smoke, which the spec explicitly treats as non-blocking and the docs describe accurately.
strengths: `src/lib/render.js`, `src/main.js`, and `src/styles.css` now place the saved-player loader in a separate sidebar, default it to collapsed, keep the toolbar visible while collapsed, and render saved players as compact one-line rows with a dedicated row-body selection target and isolated delete button.

Core behavior remains intact from code inspection plus verification: header/headerless parsing, exact-10 load gating, local-storage save/load/delete flows, 6 candidate generation, `1탱 2딜 2힐` slot structure, candidate selection, and two-click swap editing.

Independent runtime checks confirmed the sample fixture still produces 113400 valid assignments, surfaces exactly 6 candidates, preserves ordering by total diff -> role diff sum -> tank diff -> unranked diff, and keeps candidates free of duplicate player assignment.
Rendered result HTML still hides score-oriented UI labels while preserving Korean product copy, compact candidate cards, team labels, and preference-point controls.
`README.md` and `FINAL_OUTPUT.md` are aligned with the shipped behavior and truthfully disclose that `npm run test:browser` was not completed in this sandbox because Chromium is unavailable.
verification_run: `npm run test:browser` (fails in this sandbox: Chromium-family browser not installed)
`node --input-type=module` script verifying sample-fixture candidate count, top-6 ordering, uniqueness, role shape, and preference-driven tie-bucket changes
`node --input-type=module` script rendering `renderResult(...)` to confirm 6 candidate buttons and absence of score labels
release_readiness: Release-ready for this iteration. Residual risk is limited to unexecuted real-browser smoke in this environment, but that gap is explicitly documented and is non-blocking under the current spec.
